sections.h2: Which Bakersville offices run Mitchell County property tax?
sections.html:
An assessor and a collector share the job, in adjoining buildings on Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville. Doors open at 8:00 and shut at 4:30, Monday through Friday.

  • Assessor: Suite 5 at number 26, phone 828.688.2139 extension 1407. Staff there list, value and assess real and personal property.
  • Collector: number 61, phone 828.537.1627. Staff there mail bills and accept money.

The assessor also handles applications for relief, exemptions, exclusions and Present Use Value. Seven fire districts levy a tax that the collector includes on the bill, so the charges you see depend on where your parcel lies.

sections.h2: What is Mitchell County's size and housing profile?
sections.html:
Mitchell County has 15,062 residents for July 2025. That is up a little from the 14,903 counted in 2020 and below the 15,579 of 2010. The county's 221.25 land square miles give it a density near 67 per square mile.

Housing units number 8,785. Owners live in 76.3 percent of the homes, with a mid-range value of $220,100 in the survey covering 2020 to 2024. Rent runs $813 at the median, households number 6,587, and the commute averages 24.4 minutes. Builders took out 44 permits in 2025.

Work is modest in scale: 371 employer establishments employed 4,297 people in 2023, while 1,202 businesses had no employees. About 56.2 percent of adults hold or seek jobs, while seniors make up 27.6 percent of the population. Those older owners are the reason the relief programs below matter locally.

sections.h2: What is the Mitchell County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Payment opens at the September 1 due date, and the county adds nothing until after January 5. Delinquency starts January 6 with a charge of 2 percent, then 0.75 percent more each additional month. Any due date falling on a Saturday or Sunday rolls forward to Monday's business day.

Calendar from the Mitchell County Tax Collector's page
Time of yearStep
January 1Assessment date
JanuaryListing month for changes
JulyCurrent bills processed
AugustBills mailed to January 1 owner of record
September 1Payment due
January 5Last interest-free day
FebruaryDelinquent notices go out
MarchDelinquent list advertised

The state rule behind the interest-free cutoff is G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: Where and how do Mitchell County taxpayers pay?
sections.html:
At the Tax Office you can hand over cash, a check, or a debit or credit card. The county's online portal lives at mitchell.webtaxpay.com and takes cards or e-checks, with a convenience fee kept by the vendor running it.

Monthly installments are allowed on current taxes. Delinquent balances can also be spread out, but only after a payment agreement is signed. Anyone already late should phone 828.537.1627 before the March newspaper advertisement.

The collector gives sellers a clear instruction: the August mailing goes to the person who owned on January 1, so your attorney's closing papers should show how the year was settled. If you sold mid-year, expect your name on it anyway.

sections.h2: What must a Mitchell County owner report during January?
sections.html:
Changes to land, buildings or taxable personal property are reported in January. The commissioners can stretch that window, and the assessor warns of a 10 percent penalty for property listed late. The authority is G.S. 105-307.

The assessor's page names these taxable items:

  • business assets,
  • untagged vehicles,
  • boats and personal watercraft,
  • untagged campers and trailers,
  • mobile homes,
  • aircraft.

Print the forms, complete them and mail them to Suite 5. Current versions are published by the state revenue department. New construction, a removed outbuilding or a newly placed manufactured home are changes worth reporting.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Mitchell County valuation?
sections.html:
Value complaints go to the equalization board, which is the commissioners themselves unless the county has appointed a separate panel. Under G.S. 105-322 it holds its first meeting no sooner than April's first Monday and no later than May's.

  • Ask for a hearing, by letter or in person, ahead of adjournment.
  • A late-mailed notice, one sent under 15 days before adjournment, gives you 15 days from the mailing.
  • The decision arrives by mail within 30 days after adjournment.
  • Taking the case to the Property Tax Commission requires a filing inside 30 days (G.S. 105-290).

Counties must reappraise real estate at least once every eight years, and in a reappraisal year the board stays in session until December 1. Ask the assessor when your parcel was last reappraised and when the next cycle falls.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs fit Mitchell County owners?
sections.html:
North Carolina runs three programs and lets an owner use only one. Mitchell County owners apply through the assessor with Form AV-9.

  • Age or disability exclusion: at least $25,000 off, or half the value if that is greater, for owners 65 or over or permanently disabled whose 2026 income is $38,800 or less.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off value, and no age or income cutoff. Form NCDVA-9 is filled out first with a Veterans Service Officer, and the Census Bureau counts 946 veterans here.
  • Circuit breaker: bills capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for income up to $58,200 in 2026, once you have lived in the home five years. File again each year.

Anything deferred under the circuit breaker is owed once the house is sold or no longer lived in, so sellers need the deferred total from the assessor. The details appear in G.S. 105-277.1B.

sections.h2: What can a Mitchell County seller do about a bill before closing?
sections.html:
Start with the Tax Collector at 828.537.1627. Ask for the balance on the current year and on any past year, and ask whether an installment plan or payment agreement is active. A closing attorney needs a written payoff, not an estimate.

Then call the Tax Assessor at extension 1407 and ask whether the parcel carries an exclusion or a deferred circuit breaker balance, since a deferral comes due at transfer. Collect your own paperwork too: the last bill, any AV-9 you filed, and the deed that put the house in your name.

Owners who list property for the first time or add buildings are expected to report them in January, so confirm that recent additions are on the record before a buyer's appraiser sees them.

sections.h2: What happens if Mitchell County taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
The lien dates from the January 1 listing date and brings penalties and costs with it (G.S. 105-355). A foreclosure suit under G.S. 105-374 ends in an auction at the courthouse door.

That sale takes time. The commissioner reports the sale in three days, and any raised bid or objection must arrive within 10 days of that report. Until the court confirms, a person redeeming pays the taxes, penalty, interest and cost charges. An owner who closes first still negotiates the price.

For a Mitchell County seller the order of operations is short: ask the collector for a payoff, check with the assessor for relief or deferral on the parcel, and pass both numbers to the closing attorney. Where repairs are out of reach, a written cash offer for the property as is can fit that schedule.

faqs.q: When does interest begin on a Mitchell County bill?
faqs.a: January 6. The final interest-free day is January 5. After that the charge is 2 percent for the first month and 0.75 percent for every later month.

faqs.q: Where is the walk-in payment counter?
faqs.a: At the Tax Collector's counter, 61 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, any weekday between 8:00 and 4:30. It takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards.

faqs.q: Who answers questions on my assessment or exemption form?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor handles both, at 828.688.2139 extension 1407. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 5.

faqs.q: May I pay my bill in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, in monthly payments on the current year's tax. Late balances qualify too once you sign a payment agreement.

faqs.q: What happens if I forget to list property in January?
faqs.a: The assessor says a 10 percent penalty is added. The regular window is the month of January unless the commissioners extend it.
